answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer:
No. Stick to your usual three days and don't add the two you missed. You had a fever only a few days ago and you're still coughing and wiped out, so your body is still getting over it.

Squeezing five sessions into one week would pile on work just when you can handle it least. Missed runs don't need to be paid back. You'll lose almost nothing by having a lighter week now, but rushing could cost you more time.

Next week is a walk on Monday, then two walk-runs. Wednesday's is shorter than usual. Saturday's goes back to your usual level, but only if Wednesday went well. If the cough is clearing, you start building again in the week of Sep 21.

new.analysis:
**How the week went against the plan**
You did Monday exactly as planned, then the cold took the rest of the week. That was 8 runs of 2 minutes with 1-minute walks in between: 24 minutes and 2.78 km. You skipped Wednesday and Saturday because of the fever, which was the right call.

**Monday's heart rate**
On Monday your heart rate was higher than the week before at about the same pace. The cold showed up the next day, so it may already have been starting.

| Run | Average heart rate | Time in zone 3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mon Aug 31 | 133 | 33% |
| Wed Sep 2 | 132 | 24% |
| Sat Sep 5 | 136 | 45% |
| Mon Sep 7 | 139 | 83% |

This gives you a useful check as you come back. If the running bits feel harder than before, or your heart rate is higher at the same pace, take that as a sign to ease off.

**Why next week is lighter**
Getting over the cold comes before training. Hard running while you're still fighting a cold tends to make it drag on longer. Three weeks of steady walk-runs won't disappear in one quieter week.

**How the week is built**
The week starts below your usual level and only climbs back if the early sessions go well. Each run has a fallback, so on a bad day you walk rather than push through. Keeping the effort easy matters more than finishing every running bit.

**Where this leaves the race**
You can still be ready for Nov 15, but the plan won't rush to make up the lost week. Once the cough clears, the running bits will get longer step by step through late September and October. Pushing harder now could set you back further than one quiet week does.

**Why there are no faster sessions**
The plan sticks with easy walk-runs, even though you're in the part of the plan where the training builds. A few weeks into running, building means longer running bits, not speed. Faster running can wait until you can run 20 minutes or more without stopping.
